challenges.name: vertical-slice-crash-and-redelivery
challenges.title: A vertical slice: where a crash or a redelivery changes the result
challenges.description: Two pieces of the CodeDev slice POST /lessons/:lessonId/complete -> progress service -> event bus -> leaderboard consumer, with a crash in the middle. For each, decide whether the statement about what happens next is true.

questions.explanation: True. This is the dual-write problem. PostgreSQL committed, then the process stopped before bus.publish ran, and nothing records that a publish is still owed: a retry finds the lesson already completed and publishes nothing. The leaderboard (and the certificate service, which listens to the same events) silently drifts from PostgreSQL. Moving the publish inside the transaction does not fix it: the message could go out and the transaction then roll back. The outbox closes the gap by writing the event as a row in the same transaction, so the commit records both or neither, and a relay publishes it afterwards, at least once. The misconception is that a gap of a few milliseconds is too small to matter: deploys, OOM kills and spot reclaims land in exactly that gap every day at 20,000 daily active learners.

False. It is the other way round. If the consumer dies after SADD and before ZINCRBY, the event id is already marked as processed but the points were never added. The bus redelivers the message (it was never acked), SADD now returns 0 and the consumer skips it: the points are lost for good. Swapping the two commands gives the opposite failure (a crash after ZINCRBY and before SADD counts the event twice on redelivery). No order of two separate commands is safe; they have to run as one atomic step, such as a Lua script or MULTI/EXEC that does the SADD and the ZINCRBY together. The misconception is that "check, then write" is idempotent by itself: it is idempotent only when the check and the write commit together.

challenges.name: vertical-slice-idempotent-end-to-end
challenges.title: Vertical slice: API to leaderboard, idempotent end to end
challenges.description:
Build the CodeDev vertical slice for "complete a lesson": the API handler and progress service write the progress and an outbox event in one PostgreSQL transaction, a relay publishes the outbox to the event bus, and the leaderboard consumer adds the points to a Redis sorted set. Clients retry, the relay can die between publishing and marking a row, and the bus delivers at least once, so every hop must be idempotent: the same request retried returns the same response and changes nothing twice, a redelivered event counts once, and a crash at any step converges after the replay.

Write three functions (the fakes are in the file; use only the interfaces given):
1) completeLesson(req, ctx) -> ApiResponse. a) requestId, userId and lessonId must be non-empty strings, else { status: 400, error: "invalid_request" }. b) Everything else in ONE ctx.store.transaction, with the idempotency key "<userId>/<requestId>" (each client picks its request ids, so they are unique per learner only). If a request is saved under the key with the same lessonId, return its saved response unchanged; with another lessonId, return { status: 422, error: "request_id_reused" }. If lessonId is not an own key of ctx.lessonPoints (the server's catalog: the client never sends points), return { status: 404, error: "unknown_lesson" } and save nothing. If the learner already completed the lesson, respond { status: 200, lessonId, newlyCompleted: false, totalPoints } and change nothing else. Otherwise append lessonId to progress.completed, add its points, append the outbox event { eventId: "lesson-completed:<userId>:<lessonId>", userId, lessonId, points } and respond { status: 200, lessonId, newlyCompleted: true, totalPoints } (totalPoints after the change). Save every 200 response with tx.putRequest(key, { lessonId, response }) in the same transaction. A learner without a progress row starts at { completed: [], points: 0 }. Let exceptions from the store propagate (a crash must stay a crash).
2) relayOutbox(ctx): for each row of ctx.store.unpublished() (seq order), ctx.bus.publish(row.event), then ctx.store.markPublished(row.seq).
3) onLessonCompleted(event, ctx): in one ctx.board.atomically call, return if board.isProcessed(event.eventId); otherwise markProcessed(event.eventId) and incrementBy(event.userId, event.points).

Input: { lessonPoints, script }. Script steps: { request, crash? } calls completeLesson; crash "beforeCommit" kills the process just before its first transaction commits (nothing is saved), "afterCommit" right after it commits (saved, but the client gets no response). { relay: true, crashAtPublish?: N, crashAfterPublish?: N } runs relayOutbox; the process dies at the Nth publish of that step, before or after the message reaches the bus. { deliver: true, crashBeforeAck?: N } delivers the bus queue in order; the process dies after handling the Nth message and before its ack, so that message stays at the head of the queue. After the script, a final replay runs relayOutbox and delivers the whole queue with no crash.
Output (JSON): responses (one per request step: the response, or "connection lost"), progress per learner (completed sorted, points), events (outbox event ids in seq order), board ([userId, points], highest first, ties by userId) and errors (unexpected exceptions).
hints: For each crash point, ask what the next attempt finds. If the process dies right after the commit, which rows exist, and what must the retry with the same requestId find so that it can answer exactly what the first attempt would have answered?

Look at what goes into the single transaction of completeLesson: the progress, the outbox event and the saved response must all be written there, in one commit. In the consumer, the processed check, the mark and the increment belong inside one atomically call. In the relay, ask which order of publish and markPublished can lose an event and which can only duplicate it.

A similar slice for a course purchase: key "<userId>/<checkoutId>"; one transaction reads the saved checkout (same cart: return the saved answer; another cart: 422), otherwise inserts the order, an outbox row { eventId: "order-paid:ord_17" } and the saved answer. The receipt-email consumer keeps a set of sent event ids, and checks and adds to it in the same atomic step that queues the email.

tests.name: Three learners complete lessons once each: responses, progress, outbox events and board
The response is lost after the commit: the retry with the same request id gets the same answer
Crash before the commit: nothing is saved and the retry completes the lesson once
Relay dies after publishing and the consumer dies before its ack: each event counts once
Relay dies before the message reaches the bus: the event is still delivered after the replay
Request ids are per learner, a reused id for another lesson is 422, a replay keeps its first answer
Invalid requests: 400 for missing or non-string ids, 404 for an unknown lesson, nothing saved
Large input: 90 learners, about 500 steps with retries, crashes, relay and consumer failures
